passages.title: Transition.
passages.text: Paul requests prayer for his work, reassures them of God’s faithfulness, and closes by praying for them.
Paul asks them to pray that **the word of the Lord** (the gospel) would **speed ahead** (progress) and **be honored** (by people accepting its truth).
**guard you against the evil one**. Satan has been trying to destroy the Thessalonians’ young faith. But God’s faithfulness assures Paul that the Evil One will not succeed.

passages.title: The Problem of Lazy Christians.
passages.text: Paul instructs the Thes­salonians to discipline those refusing to work.
The missionaries had taught the need to work for a living both by example and through instruction.

**eat anyone’s bread without paying for it**. Paul refused to depend on others for his living. He took on manual labor in addition to his ministry commitments to avoid being a financial** burden** to the Thessalonians. He did so even though he had the God-given **right** to be supported (see 1 Cor. 9:3–15 ; 1 Thess. 2:9 ).

passages.title: Conclusion.
passages.text: The letter concludes with a blessing, a final greeting, and a prayer for grace.

notes.text: **the steadfastness of Christ**. Either Christ’s endurance as a model for Christians or the perseverance Christ gives to believers.

Paul tells the Thessalonians to discipline those who refuse to work and depend on others to support them. They are to **keep away from** these people, which probably means removing them from the church. However, Paul still regards them as “brothers” (v. 15 ). This behavior was **not in accord with the tradition** passed on by the missionaries regarding the necessity of working for a living.
**not busy at work, but busybodies**. See 1 Tim. 5:13 .
**do not** **grow weary in doing good**. Paul encourages those with money to continue being charitable, though only to those who are deserving.
The purpose of keeping away from the lazy is so these brothers will **be ashamed**, repent, and be restored to the community.
**Lord of peace**. Jesus has reconciled Christians to God. He is able to replace their fear ( 2:2 ) with peace.
Paul makes it clear that most of the letter was dictated to a secretary. The final **greeting** was written in Paul’s own handwriting. This served as a mark of its authenticity.
